is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.s., Anopheles arabiensis, and Anopheles funestus s.s. (Abstract, page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for the Vgsc L1014S (kdr-east) mutation in Anopheles gambiae s.s., An. arabiensis, and An. funestus s.s. (Table 1, Table 6).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 and Table 6 provide the number of mosquitoes genotyped (N) and the allelic frequency (AF %) and percentage of homozygous (RR %) for the L1014S mutation.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in the Suba district, Nyanza province, western Kenya (Materials and Methods, page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original empirical study reporting new field data and bioassays.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides data at the village/site level (e.g., Nyaroya, Nyandago, Mirunda, etc.) in the Suba district, Nyanza province, Kenya (Table 1, Table 6).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were performed between 2009 and 2011 (Materials and Methods, page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes original field collections conducted by the authors between 2009 and 2011.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including genotype counts and frequencies, are provided in the main text tables.

assessment.summary: This study investigated pyrethroid resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.s., An. arabiensis, and An. funestus s.s. in western Kenya. It combined larval and adult bioassays with genotyping for the L1014S kdr mutation. High frequencies of L1014S were found in An. gambiae s.s., while it was absent in An. arabiensis and An. funestus s.s., which instead showed evidence of metabolic resistance.
